checks: For any convex combination of positive fibers at an integer base z, convexity gives a Minkowski subset of K_z. A nonnegative weighted sum of positive homothetic copies of one convex K has radius equal to the weighted sum, which is positive. Thus z is a positive-volume base even if its status is not assumed beforehand, and volume comparison gives the anchored radius inequality.

For each sampled p the feasible primal weights form a nonempty compact subset of a simplex and have objective at most r_p, attained by the point mass. The constant-majorant dual is feasible, and finite LP duality gives an attained affine majorant at p on the affine base span. This also works for boundary and rank-zero bases. The contact hyperplane contains the minimal face F_p and base projection is injective on it. If the whole hull is affine, its contact face may be the whole hull as allowed.

Exact set equality implies exact midpoint radius equality because d is positive and the reference volume is nonzero. A face containing the midpoint includes both endpoints, so both endpoint minimal faces lie in the parent minimal face. Iterating over any terminating path covers its nodes and every partner root. In the finite family each root face lies in a maximal one.

A face of a finite convex hull is generated by the sampled points it contains. At any integer z in its projection the lift is a convex combination on the supporting graph. The anchored inequality gives positivity and radius at least the majorant value, while the majorant gives the reverse inequality after z is recognized as sampled. Injectivity then identifies the actual lift with the given lift in the face.

When a convex combination of projected patch bases lands at an integer patch base, the Minkowski subset has exactly the target radius. Proper inclusion of two full-dimensional compact convex bodies would leave a positive-volume ball, by density of the larger body’s interior, so the sets are equal. Taking centroids is valid because K has centroid zero.

The root projects into the relative interior of its patch. For each sampled base, a small positive coefficient there leaves a residual point in the projected polytope. Averaging produces one representation of the root with all coefficients strictly positive. Both signs of a small perturbation along any affine dependence then give valid anchored identities. Subtraction shows that the centroid data annihilate every affine dependence, giving the affine extension on the full patch span, including singleton patches.

Verified the source bytes and §§1–3, (1)–(8), in 39e0ea36e1546d5b. Section 2 explicitly says termination and exact set equality suffice for face filtration, so dropping volume maximality from the normalized hypotheses is faithful. The draft proves its own anchored inequality using homothety.

overlap.comparison: The accepted touching affine support majorants at u and −u can be added and divided by the positive width of K to give the radius majorant in this setting. It supplies neither forest face filtration nor patchwise centroid affinity.

Accepted anchored support compatibility and its affine singleton lineality use the same affine-dependence argument. The latter starts from a lineality element, while this result constructs the relevant complete patches of positive bodies and derives their centroid identities.

The accepted lattice-completeness statement concerns a full positive contact set of an ordinary maximal-depth-root majorant. It does not describe minimal terminal-root radius faces, their path inclusions, or the actual centroids on them.

readability: The minimal-face convention and the positivity step at an integer target make the boundary cases clear. Terminal-root faces may overlap. No aggregate patch weight or depth statement enters the proof.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Exact set equalities on a terminating prescribed forest give face inclusion and a cover by minimal terminal-root faces. Each such face projects injectively, contains every integer base in its projection, and carries affine radii and actual centroids.
